title: Professor Mari server-side authorization gate (removed in 2.4.6)
skill_evidence: SKILL.md:122 'and a server-side gate that lets her change data only when the user explicitly asked for that edit (2.4.3), with Keep/Restore review cards as the second line'; SKILL.md:153 'Independently, a server-side gate (2.4.3) lets her change data only when the active request explicitly asked for that edit — so phrase a build request as an instruction ("create a lorebook with…"), not a musing.'
reality: CHANGELOG 2.4.6 line 1273 (#5721): 'the server-side authorization gate added after #4838 ... is removed. An intent-authorized edit now lands directly in the existing Keep/Restore review card' (the gate was #5093, 2.4.3, line 1599). No excerpt-binding gate remains under packages/server/src/services/professor-mari/ at v2.5.0; what remains is prompt-level read-only guidance for 'how do I…' questions (workspace-agent.service.ts:657; #4816/#4838), Plan mode's server-side refusal (#5725), the ask-then-Accept hold (#5748, #5820) and Keep/Restore cards. references/architecture.md:111 already says the gate was removed in v2.4.6, so SKILL.md also contradicts its own reference.
fix: SKILL.md:122 — replace the gate clause with 'the 2.4.3 server-side authorization gate (#5093) was removed in 2.4.6 (#5721): intent-phrased edits land straight in a Keep/Restore card'. SKILL.md:153 — replace 'Independently, a server-side gate (2.4.3)… not a musing.' with 'She treats "how do I…" questions as read-only and answers them, while an instruction — even a polite "can you set X to Y" — is carried out; once she asks whether to apply, later edits wait behind Accept / Don't apply (#5748). (The 2.4.3 server-side authorization gate was removed in 2.4.6, #5721.)' Keep the 'check the Permissions Mode first' advice.

title: Share requests with other agents — batching misdated to 2.5.0
skill_evidence: SKILL.md:112 '↺ "Share requests with other agents" is on by default (#6977): agents are batched into shared requests, so "N agents = N+1 calls" no longer holds'; SKILL.md:222 'Since 2.5.0, agents also share requests by default, so several agents no longer mean one call each'; SKILL.md:233 '(Share requests with other agents, on by default since 2.5.0)'; references/decision-guide.md:164 '(on by default since 2.5.0) batches agents into shared calls'
reality: CHANGELOG 2.5.0 line 152 (#6977): the agent editor gets a NEW switch that lets an agent opt OUT ('Turn it off to send that agent in its own request instead of together with other agents… It is on by default'). Batching itself predates 2.5.0: 2.0.9 line 2758 ('keeping compatible agents batched'), 2.4.2 line 1742 (#4950, 'post-processing Agent batches'), 2.4.2 line 1899 (#4614, 'during batching'). references/agents.md:406 already frames it correctly ('Corrected at the v2.5.0 sync — earlier guidance said every enabled agent is a separate LLM call'; only the switch is v2.5.0).
fix: Reword all four places: 'Agents that share a connection have long been batched into shared requests (the old "N agents = N+1 calls" rule was never right); 2.5.0 (#6977) added a per-agent Share requests with other agents switch (on by default) to opt one out, e.g. for a local model that mixes up tasks.' In SKILL.md:222/233 and decision-guide.md:164 drop 'since 2.5.0' from the batching default and attribute only the switch to 2.5.0.

title: Character-ID macros described as 'narrowed' in 2.5.0
skill_evidence: SKILL.md:109 '↺ Character-ID macros narrowed (#6956). {{<cardId>}} now resolves to the name everywhere, but adds the referenced card's context only in Roleplay chats that use a prompt preset.'; SKILL.md:136 '(Narrowed in 2.5.0 — see above.)'
reality: CHANGELOG 2.5.0 line 167 (#6956): ID macros 'now become the character's name in Conversation and Game chats, and in Roleplay chats without a preset, instead of staying as raw text' — 2.5.0 widened name resolution; those chats never received the card context because the macro was not resolved there at all. Line 188 (#6924) also resolves the name when the character is already in the chat (card still sent once). The context-loading behavior from #4336 (2.4.0, line 1950) was not reduced.
fix: SKILL.md:109 — 'Character-ID macros resolve more widely (#6956, #6924): {{<cardId>}} now becomes the name in Conversation, Game and preset-less Roleplay (previously left as raw text) and when that character is already in the chat. The referenced card's context is added only in Roleplay chats that use a prompt preset — the skill's v2.4.0 wording implied every mode.' Keep ↺ only as a correction of the skill's own earlier guidance; change SKILL.md:136 to '(Scope clarified in 2.5.0 — see above.)'

title: Whisper listed as a 2.4.6 Roleplay Command
skill_evidence: references/decision-guide.md:106-107 '**Roleplay Commands** (2.4.6, Chat Settings → Agents → Roleplay Commands; each one starts **off**)… **Whisper** — private asides and secrets that only the recipient and the narrator receive.'
reality: CHANGELOG 2.5.0 line 491 (#6616): 'Roleplay's optional Whisper command shares an inline secret only with its recipient and the appointed narrator. Recipients can be characters or your persona'. 2.5.0 also lets users write whisper/notes commands in their own messages (line 236) and in edited character/narrator messages (#6918, line 199). The 2.4.6 Roleplay Commands entry (line 983) has no Whisper.
fix: decision-guide.md:107 — tag it: '**Whisper** (2.5.0, #6616) — a private aside only the recipient (a character or your persona) and the appointed narrator receive; you can also type whispers in your own messages.'

title: Text-format <tool_call> parsing dated to 2.5.0
skill_evidence: references/decision-guide.md:334 'Setups that emit tool calls as plain `<tool_call>…</tool_call>` text (some KoboldCPP / Gemma configurations) are parsed and run since 2.5.0.'
reality: CHANGELOG 2.0.3 line 3003: 'Fixed local-provider textual tool calls so local models, including Gemma-style delimiter output, can be repaired into supported tool calls'. 2.5.0 #6951 (line 165) only fixed streaming: the raw tool-call text no longer appears in a streamed reply and is not saved, 'the same as with streaming off'.
fix: decision-guide.md:334 — 'Setups that emit tool calls as plain <tool_call>…</tool_call> text (some KoboldCPP / Gemma configurations) are recognised and run; since 2.5.0 (#6951) that raw text also stays out of streamed replies.'

title: Sandboxed-extension capability list omits estimateTextTokens
skill_evidence: SKILL.md:214 'A sandboxed Browser Extension gets private storage, logging, timers, the fixed UI control set, and a read-only snapshot of active chat/character IDs — plus bounded card fields only with approved read_active_characters / read_active_persona permissions.'
reality: CHANGELOG 2.5.0 line 838 (#6257): 'Personal Extensions can use Marinara's built-in text token estimator through marinara.estimateTextTokens(text)'. references/extensions.md:83 and :195 list it (no capability needed). The SKILL.md list reads as exhaustive, so a model would wrongly say an extension can't estimate tokens.
fix: SKILL.md:214 — add 'the built-in text token estimator (marinara.estimateTextTokens, 2.5.0)' to the list of what a sandboxed Browser Extension gets.
